note: Race metadata for the 2026 Austin City Council cycle. Each entry drives one race view page at /austin/<race_id>/ via race_template.html. Adding a district = add one entry here + run build_race.py --race <race_id>. Candidate stats are on a common 2026-cycle basis (contributions from 2025-01-01 forward) so candidates who have run before are compared on this race only, not lifetime totals. Post-election fields (all optional; older entries without them render as before): race.phase = filing | ballot_set | runoff | decided (absent -> ballot_set when ballot_final is true, else filing); race.result_note = one sentence of framing shown in the outcome banner; race.result_source = {outlet, url, date} linked from that banner; race.runoff_early_voting = 'YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD' (runoff phase only); candidate.result = won | runoff | eliminated (absent = still running); candidate.vote_pct = number, omit unless a reported figure is on hand.

races.title: Austin City Council District 1
races.result_note: Goodwin and Ramos each took just over a third of the vote on Nov 3 and advance to a Dec 12 runoff; results are unofficial until the canvass.
races.intro: District 1 is an open seat. Natasha Harper-Madison, who has represented the district since 2019, is not seeking a third term. Austin's two-term limit permits a third term if a member gathers signatures from 5% of registered voters in the district; Harper-Madison declined to pursue that petition. Her term ends January 6, 2027. On November 3, 2026, Amber Goodwin and Misael Ramos finished as the top two in a six-candidate field, each with just over a third of the vote; with no one clearing 50 percent, they meet in a December 12 runoff.
races.context_note: Filing closed August 17, 2026 with six candidates on the ballot. Money raised for the December 12 runoff is reported in the same City Clerk filings and is included here as reports post.

candidates.name: Amber Goodwin
candidates.bio: Assistant district attorney in the Travis County DA's office; founder of the Community Justice Action Fund and former chair of Austin's Gun Violence Prevention Task Force.

candidates.name: Misael Ramos
candidates.bio: Community organizer and affordable-housing development professional; president of the Rogers Washington-Holy Cross Neighborhood Association. Ran for this seat in 2022, finishing second.

candidates.name: Alexandria Anderson
candidates.bio: Small-business owner and certified personal trainer; retired Nike-sponsored sprinter and UT graduate; president of the MLK Neighborhood Association.

candidates.name: Steven Brown
candidates.bio: Born and raised in East Austin; clinical specialist for medical-technology firm Medtronic. Formerly a co-chair of the Save Austin Now PAC.

candidates.name: Portia Riggins
candidates.bio: Third-generation East Austinite raised near 12th & Airport; background in accounting, finance and administration; finishing an associate's degree at Austin Community College.

candidates.name: Michael Nahas
candidates.bio: Computer science and economics background; housing-supply advocate.
candidates.placeholder_note: Filed every required campaign finance report but has reported no itemized contributions.

races.title: Austin City Council District 3
races.result_note: Incumbent Velásquez led with 47.3 percent on Nov 3 but fell short of a majority and faces Shah, who took 24.7 percent, in a Dec 12 runoff; results are unofficial until the canvass.
races.intro: José Velásquez, who has represented District 3 since 2023, is seeking a second term. He won the seat in December 2022, defeating Daniela Silva in a runoff with 53% of the vote. The district covers Central-East and East Austin. On November 3, 2026, Velásquez led a five-candidate field with 47.3 percent of the vote, short of the majority needed to win outright; he meets second-place finisher Neha Shah, who took 24.7 percent, in a December 12 runoff.
races.context_note: Filing closed August 17, 2026 with five candidates on the ballot. Money raised for the December 12 runoff is reported in the same City Clerk filings and is included here as reports post.

candidates.name: José Velásquez
candidates.bio: East Austin native and marketing strategist; elected to this seat in 2022, defeating Daniela Silva in a December runoff. Led the November 3, 2026 general but fell short of a majority; faces Neha Shah in a December runoff for a second term.

candidates.name: Neha Shah
candidates.bio: Software technology developer, startup entrepreneur and bilingual children's book author; District 3 resident since 2016. First run for office.

candidates.name: Eduardo "Lalito" Romero
candidates.bio: University staff member; ran in the March 2024 Democratic primary for Texas' 37th Congressional District and for Austin City Council District 4 in November 2024.

candidates.name: Brock Skinner
candidates.bio: Background in sales, marketing and business development; studied at the University of Texas at Austin. Campaigned on his lack of City Hall experience and on cutting city spending.

candidates.name: Gavino Fernandez Jr.
candidates.bio: Longtime East Austin activist from the Holly neighborhood; retired, formerly chief of staff to Travis County Commissioner Marcos De Leon and a LULAC district director. Ran for this seat in 2022, finishing fifth.
candidates.placeholder_note: Ran for this seat in 2022 ($5,303 raised then) but has reported no itemized contributions in the 2026 cycle.

races.title: Austin City Council District 5
races.intro: Ryan Alter, who has represented District 5 since 2023, is seeking a second term. He won the seat in December 2022, defeating Stephanie Bazan in a runoff with 60% of the vote. The district covers South-Central Austin. Note: figures here cover reported contributions only — David Weinberg has additionally loaned his campaign $275,000, which does not appear in contribution filings.
races.context_note: Candidate filing runs July 20 - August 17, 2026. Everyone listed here has declared and appointed a campaign treasurer, but filing has not closed. Expect additions, and expect some listed candidates not to complete filing.

candidates.name: Ryan Alter
candidates.bio: Attorney and former Texas Senate policy staffer; elected to this seat in 2022, defeating Stephanie Bazan in a December runoff. Seeking a second term.

candidates.name: David Weinberg
candidates.bio: Public-affairs consultant; former executive director of the Texas League of Conservation Voters and leader of the Save Zilker Park PAC. Barton Hills resident.

candidates.name: Farrah Abraham
candidates.bio: Television personality and Austin business owner; initially filed for mayor before entering the District 5 race in January 2026.
candidates.placeholder_note: Filed to run - no campaign finance data on file yet

races.title: Austin City Council District 8
races.intro: Paige Ellis, who has represented District 8 since 2019, is seeking a rare third term. Austin's two-term limit permits a third term only if a member gathers signatures from 5% of registered voters in the district — roughly 3,000 for District 8 — and her campaign began collecting them in June; the petition is due with her ballot application by August 17. She won the seat in a December 2018 runoff and was re-elected outright in 2022 with 58% of the vote. The district covers Southwest Austin. Note: figures here cover reported contributions only — Ellis has loaned her campaign about $30,000 and Selena Xie about $25,000; loans do not appear in contribution filings.
races.context_note: Candidate filing runs July 20 - August 17, 2026. Everyone listed here has declared and appointed a campaign treasurer, but filing has not closed. Expect additions, and expect some listed candidates not to complete filing.

candidates.name: Paige Ellis
candidates.bio: Environmental and public-relations professional; won this seat in a December 2018 runoff and was re-elected in 2022. Seeking a third term by petition.

candidates.name: Selena Xie
candidates.bio: Austin-Travis County EMS commander, ICU nurse and longtime president of the Austin EMS Association. First run for office.

candidates.name: Jeffery Bowen
candidates.bio: Retired Air Force veteran and construction manager; president of the Austin Neighborhoods Council and chair of the Board of Adjustment. Ran for mayor in 2024.

candidates.name: Daniel Hudsky
candidates.bio: Army veteran and 40-year Austin resident; running as the field's conservative voice.
candidates.placeholder_note: Filed to run - no campaign finance data on file yet

races.title: Austin City Council District 9
races.intro: Zohaib “Zo” Qadri, who has represented District 9 since 2023, is seeking a second term. He won the open seat in 2022, defeating Linda Guerrero with 51% of the vote in a December runoff. The district covers central Austin, including the University of Texas and West Campus.
races.context_note: Candidate filing runs July 20 - August 17, 2026. Everyone listed here has declared and appointed a campaign treasurer, but filing has not closed. Expect additions, and expect some listed candidates not to complete filing.

candidates.name: Zohaib Qadri
candidates.bio: Austin's first South Asian council member; won this seat in 2022, defeating Linda Guerrero in a December runoff. Seeking a second term.

candidates.name: Richard Heyman
candidates.bio: Urban geographer who taught urban studies at the University of Texas for two decades; District 9 homeowner since 2006. First run for office.

candidates.name: Katie Kam
candidates.bio: Civil and transportation engineer, former city urban planner and AISD science teacher; Austin resident since 1983. First run for office.

candidates.name: Dave Thadani
candidates.bio: University of Texas computer science student running on renter protections and affordable housing.

omitted.name: Ard Ardalan
omitted.reason: Suspended his campaign in December 2025 after raising $7,600. His treasurer appointment remains on file; he will be restored to the page if he re-enters before filing closes.
